key_insight: A reduced-basis hybrid ML framework combining TBNN and UDEs can learn frame-invariant viscoelastic constitutive laws from shear data and generalize to more complex flow regimes.
engineering_relevance: This enables data-driven digital twins for viscoelastic fluids that can be embedded directly into CFD solvers for rheology-aware prediction and design.
method: Train hybrid TBNN/UDE constitutive models on synthetic oscillatory shear datasets from established viscoelastic laws.
Use a reduced-dimensional tensor basis to improve physical consistency and numerical stability.
Embed the learned constitutive response into an open-source finite-volume solver for runtime evaluation from local flow conditions.
evidence_signal: Models were tested by extrapolating from shear-only training to extensional, 2D, and 3D benchmark flows including a sudden contraction and cross-slot, with accuracy improving when first normal stress difference information was included.
watch_item: Performance degrades as extrapolation increases, so strong out-of-distribution flows and high Deborah numbers remain a key reliability risk.
paper_title: Harnessing Machine Learning for Hybrid Constitutive Modelling of Viscoelastic Fluid Flows in Computational Rheology
